title: Field Ops Reliability Campaign — Activation Template (ignite)
content:
Purpose and scope

This is a lightweight 42-day activation template for running a cross-functional reliability campaign focused on SLO harmonization for model inference (hosted + dedicated + private). The goal: reduce P95 latency variance, stabilize P99 tail for peak traffic, and create a predictable error-budget-driven rollout cadence for model updates. This doc is intentionally pragmatic — mix of checklist, day-by-day runway, and notes-to-self for field engineers, PMs, and product partners.

Audience
- SREs, Platform, Serving Runtime, Product (Hosted API + Dedicated), Observability, Solutions Eng, Customer Success.

High-level objectives (success criteria)
1) P95 latency for text-generation endpoints within 20% of baseline across regions at 90th percentile traffic pattern.
2) P99 tail reduction: decrease P99 by >= 30% for the top 10 services contributing to customer error budget burn.
3) Implement a unified error-budget policy across Hosted/Dedicated/Private with an automated fallback route for model variants.
4) Have canary + rollback pipeline and a short playbook for on-call for inference regressions.

Quick wins (first 7 days)
- Verify instrumentation: key spans (serve.request, kvcache.hits, model.kernel.exec) exist in traces.
- Add a minimal dashboard tile for real-time error budget (rolling 24h) per route.
- Run a 2-hour synthetic workload that mirrors peak burst; capture traces and top-5 latency contributors.
- Add a temporary alert: sustained P99 > 2x baseline for 10min -> page SRE oncall.

Roles & responsibilities (working RACI)
- Campaign lead (Aisha Kapoor) — overall coordination, go/no-go decisions. (R)
- SRE ops (Jonah Reed) — signal definitions, alerts, on-call runbook edits. (A)
- Serving runtime (Ethan Liu) — kernel selection flags, batching/auto-batch experiments. (C)
- Observability (Marina Duarte) — dashboard tiles, tracing sampling rules, log retention tweaks. (C)
- Product host (Priya Menon) — priority routes, customer-impact mapping, external comms. (I)
- Solutions eng (Samir Patel) — customer-facing canary coordination and private deploy checklist. (I)

Signal definitions (must be implemented before day 7)
- Latency: P50/P95/P99 per route, broken down by model variant, region, and seq-length bucket.
- Error rate: 4xx/5xx per route, and model dropout/FATAL errors from runtime.
- Cost per token (approx): CPU/GPU utilization + token emission rate per second.
- Error budget: rolling 7d and 30d budget remaining per service.
- Health: KV cache hit ratio and stall counts, retry amplification metric.

Instrumentation checklist
- Ensure trace span names are consistent: serve.request -> runtime.dispatch -> model.exec -> kv.lookup.
- Add static tags for request_type (chat|completion|embed), sequence_len_bucket (0-128,129-512,512+), model_variant.
- Ensure logs include request_id and route_id, with sampling set to 10% for full payloads, 100% for errors.

42-day activation runway (high-level)
Week 0 (Days 0–7): prep + quick wins
- Confirm owners, signals, dashboards. Run synthetic load. Lock minimal alert thresholds.
- Deliverable: "campaign-preflight" dashboard and short triage runbook (1 pager).

Week 1 (Days 8–14): detection and baseline experiments
- Run targeted experiments: increase batching window, test KV-prefetch, toggle optimized kernels on a dev cluster.
- Observe P95/P99 shifts and document tradeoffs in the shared experiment sheet.
- Deliverable: experiment notes + decision log (keep or revert).

Week 2–3 (Days 15–28): cross-team mitigations and canary pipeline
- Implement conservative batching/queueing changes on canary traffic (start 5% traffic).
- Activate automatic fallback to lower-latency quantized model on sustained P99 or error budget exceed.
- Document rollback criteria: >25% increase in customer-visible error rate OR P99 > 2x baseline for 15 minutes.
- Deliverable: canary playbook + rollback automation (scripts/PRs).

Week 4–6 (Days 29–42): scaling and runbook hardening
- Expand canary (25% -> 50% -> 100%) following success gates.
- Conduct two tabletop drills with oncall + product comms for a simulated model regression.
- Finalize SLA-adjacent docs: error budget policy, billing/credits triggers for customers (hand-off to CS/Product).
- Deliverable: final campaign retro and handoff deck.

Runbook snippets (to copy into oncall playbook)
- Trigger: P99 > threshold for 10m AND error budget burn > 1%/h -> page oncall.
- Initial triage: check trace root causes (model.exec stalls, kernel OOM, queue-length spike).
- Quick rollback: switch routing policy to fallback variant (route flag: route.fallback=true). Confirm traffic shift and monitor for 10m.
- Post-incident: capture 3 example traces, label cause, create Jira ticket, and run a 72h observation window.

Metrics dashboards (core tiles)
- SLO health: error budget remaining (7d/30d), percentage of services within SLO.
- Latency skyline: P50/P95/P99 per route, with seq length filter.
- Resource correlation: GPU utilization vs P99 drift.
- KV cache: hit ratio and refill latency.

Automation & tooling asks (Engineering owners)
- Observability: add an error-budget tile and an auto-generated incident note stub when alert fires.
- Platform: expose a canary-weight API that accepts decimal traffic weights per route.
- Serving runtime: quick toggle to enable/disable kernel-optimizations with safe default.

Open risks & unknowns (work to track)
- Private deployments: telemetry surface area is inconsistent across customers — need a minimal telemetry contract for SLOs. Action: Solutions Eng to create a "private SLO telemetry spec" (owner: Samir).
- Quantization regressions: some models show hallucination increase at higher quant. Need guardrails (eval promptset) before broad rollout.
- Cost regressions: more aggressive batching reduces latency variance but can increase token cost on some workloads. Need cost-per-token monitoring.

Communication plan
- Internal: weekly 30-min sync (Mon) during active campaign; daily 15-min ops stand during canary escalation.
- External: CS/Product send a short status note to impacted customers at canary start and at final rollout.

Retro template (post-campaign)
- What surprised us?
- Biggest win?
- Where did we fail to observe signals early?
- Actions (owner + due date)
- Follow-ups for product/engineering/process

Quick timeline snapshot (first 14 days)
Day 0: preflight checks, dashboard + alerts, sanity synthetic load (owner: SRE ops).
Day 1–3: instrumentation fixes, trace span standardization (owner: Observability).
Day 4–7: baseline experiments (batching + kernel toggles) on dev cluster, document results.
Day 8: decide canary gating thresholds and implement canary-weight API.
Day 9–14: start canary at 5%, collect data, run tabletop with oncall.

Notes-to-self (informal)
- Keep experiment logs terse; best if each experiment is a single row in the experiment sheet with owner, hypothesis, metrics, pass/fail, and next step.
- Don't over-index on short-term P50 improvements — primary objective is P99/P95 stability for customer-facing routes.
- Be explicit about customer impact for every change (example: "hosted-api/chat route: 2 enterprise customers, weekly calls, high priority").

Linked short checklist (copy/paste)
- [ ] Confirm trace span naming and sampling rules
- [ ] Add error-budget dashboard tile per route
- [ ] Setup synthetic peak workload for 2 hours
- [ ] Create canary-weight API + test harness
- [ ] Draft one-page canary runbook for oncall
- [ ] Coordinate private deploy telemetry spec with Solutions Eng

Appendix: Useful links and references
- Minimal telemetry spec (draft): Confluence link above
- Jira tickets to track: SRE-3421 (campaign orchestration), SERVE-778 (canary-weight API)
- Slack channel: #reliability-ops for live ops chatter

End — this is a living draft. Add notes in-line, and mark items with owner initials for follow-up.
